questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish a research scientist role from a research engineer role on an alignment team?
options: The two roles are completely unrelated and never collaborate
A research engineer only works on deployment, never on research
A research scientist never writes code, while a research engineer never reads papers

A research scientist is more likely to originate research directions and own conceptual framing; a research engineer is more likely to turn ideas into working, well-tested experiments, though the line blurs constantly in practice
questions.explain: The distinction is one of emphasis, not a hard boundary — real alignment research engineer roles explicitly combine empirical research with production-quality engineering.

questions.q: Which specialization is most directly concerned with noticing when a reward signal is being gamed rather than genuinely optimized for?
options: Model card writing
Third-party red-teaming only
Evaluation design
RL and reward-modeling work
questions.explain: The RL and reward-modeling specialization involves building and auditing reward models and RL setups with close attention to reward hacking and specification gaming.

questions.q: Why does the interpretability specialization lean especially heavily on skeptical experimental design?
options: Because interpretability work requires no engineering skill at all
Because interpretability results are notoriously easy to over-interpret, so careful, skeptical design is needed to avoid drawing false conclusions from probes or circuit analysis
Because interpretability is only used for marketing purposes
Because interpretability tools never produce any usable results
questions.explain: Interpretability findings can look compelling while being misleading, so this specialization leans on research judgment and careful, skeptical experimentation.

questions.q: How does the evaluation design specialization differ in emphasis from the model-training specialization?
options: Evaluation design only applies to narrow, non-LLM models
Evaluation design is purely administrative and involves no technical skill
Evaluation design focuses on building rigorous, hard-to-game evals that other teams and governance documents depend on, rather than on running training/RL experiments directly
Evaluation design and model training are identical in every respect
questions.explain: Evaluation design is about rigorous experimental design that produces trustworthy, hard-to-game measurements, feeding into the system cards and safety cases covered earlier in this chapter.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how does the alignment research engineer skill set apply outside a frontier lab, such as at a third-party evaluation organization or safety institute?
options: Safety institutes exclusively do policy work with no technical component
Third-party organizations only need marketing and communications skills
It doesn't transfer at all outside a frontier lab
The same skills apply, but such organizations tend to emphasize evaluation-design and interpretability work more heavily since they typically don't control model training directly
questions.explain: Organizations that assess models they don't build themselves tend to lean more on rigorous, externally credible evaluation and interpretability work than on training-pipeline experimentation.
